data.long_meaning: A woman who is a jurist or scholar in Islamic law. Derived from the word 'Mujtahid' which refers to a person who has the ability to deduce religious laws from primary Islamic sources. The name Mujtahidah carries the meaning “Jurist, Scholar” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mujtahidah usually hope their child will grow to embody jurist, scholar and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The title "Mujtahidah" is a testament to the importance of women in Islamic scholarship and law. Historically, women have made significant contributions to the interpretation and application of Islamic law in various contexts, from the early Islamic period to the present day. Their scholarly achievements have not only enriched the Islamic intellectual tradition but have also challenged traditional gender roles and stereotypes. The recognition of "Mujtahidah" underscores the importance of women's intellectual and religious autonomy in Islam.
data.spiritual_significance: The title "Mujtahidah" conveys the spiritual significance of seeking knowledge and understanding in Islam, regardless of gender. It emphasizes the importance of independent reasoning and critical thinking in the pursuit of religious truth. By embracing the title, a woman identifies herself as someone who has dedicated herself to the quest for knowledge and the application of Islamic laws to her daily life, thereby embodying the ideals of piety, wisdom, and scholarship. Ultimately, the title serves as a reminder of the divine call to "seek knowledge even as far as China" and the value of intellectual curiosity and spiritual growth in Islam.
